_national.labelling: No federal appellation system: quality wine schemes are provincial (VQA Ontario under the VQA Act 1999; BC VQA and BC Wine of Distinction under B.C. Reg. 168/2018; Quebec IGPs under CARTV; Tidal Bay in Nova Scotia run by the growers' association). Federally (CFIA Standards of Identity) "Icewine", "ice wine" or "ice-wine" means wine made exclusively from grapes naturally frozen on the vine and, if made in Canada, certified so by the provincial authority.

ca-cidre-de-glace-du-quebec.varieties: Late-ripening apple varieties grown in Quebec.
ca-cidre-de-glace-du-quebec.min_alcohol: 9 to 13% abv actual; residual sugar at least 140 g/l; must at least 1.139 density (about 32 Brix) before fermentation.
ca-cidre-de-glace-du-quebec.styles: Sugar concentrated only by natural winter cold: cryoconcentration (freezing pressed juice) or cryoextraction (pressing frozen fruit, including apples frozen on the tree, which must hang until at least 1 December). No added colour or flavour; sugar and alcohol only from the apples.
ca-cidre-de-glace-du-quebec.labelling: IGP; all steps on the certified producer's main site.

ca-lake-erie-north-shore.labelling: Viticultural area: 85% from Lake Erie North Shore (Essex, Kent south of the Thames and Elgin counties, plus Pelee); its sub-appellation South Islands (Pelee Township) requires 100%.
ca-lake-erie-north-shore.styles: Icewine (Ontario): vinifera or Vidal naturally frozen on the vine, picked at minus 8 C or colder and pressed immediately in a continuous process, pressing within the viticultural area; at least 32 Brix at each pressing and 35 Brix average; residual sugar at least 100 g/l, all natural; 7.0 to 14.9% actual; no freeze concentration (grapes or must may be chilled no lower than minus 4 C); 100% from a viticultural area, at least 85% from the one named; vintage and varieties stated.

ca-niagara-peninsula.labelling: Primary viticultural area: 85% of grapes from Niagara Peninsula (vinifera only, except Vidal for Icewine), vintage required. Its regional areas Niagara-on-the-Lake, Niagara Escarpment and West Niagara need 85% from the region with the rest from Niagara Peninsula; its 10 sub-appellations need 100%. Labels may show both the sub-appellation and the larger area.
ca-niagara-peninsula.styles: Icewine (Ontario): vinifera or Vidal naturally frozen on the vine, picked at minus 8 C or colder and pressed immediately in a continuous process, pressing within the viticultural area; at least 32 Brix at each pressing and 35 Brix average; residual sugar at least 100 g/l, all natural; 7.0 to 14.9% actual; no freeze concentration (grapes or must may be chilled no lower than minus 4 C); 100% from a viticultural area, at least 85% from the one named; vintage and varieties stated.

src.title: Ontario Regulation 406/00 (VQA Ontario rules), consolidated from 6 July 2026 (last amendment O. Reg. 226/26)

ca-okanagan-valley.labelling: Regional GI: 85% from the Okanagan Valley, rest from BC (since 14 July 2025; previously 95%). Its 11 sub-GIs (Golden Mile Bench, Golden Mile Slopes, Naramata Bench, Okanagan Falls, Skaha Bench, Lake Country, East and South Kelowna Slopes, Summerland Bench, Lakefront and Valleys) carry "Okanagan Valley" too.
ca-okanagan-valley.styles: Icewine (BC VQA): vinifera or Vidal Blanc frozen naturally on the vine, picked at minus 8 C or colder and pressed while frozen in the same GI; 32 Brix per pressing, 35 Brix average; at least 100 g/l residual sugar, all natural; no sweet reserve, chaptalisation or artificial cooling below minus 4 C; VA max 2.1 g/l; varieties must be stated.

ca-prince-edward-county.labelling: Viticultural area: 85% from Prince Edward County (incl. Amherst Island and a strip of the mainland), vinifera only; vintage required.
ca-prince-edward-county.styles: Icewine (Ontario): vinifera or Vidal naturally frozen on the vine, picked at minus 8 C or colder and pressed immediately in a continuous process, pressing within the viticultural area; at least 32 Brix at each pressing and 35 Brix average; residual sugar at least 100 g/l, all natural; 7.0 to 14.9% actual; no freeze concentration (grapes or must may be chilled no lower than minus 4 C); 100% from a viticultural area, at least 85% from the one named; vintage and varieties stated.

ca-tidal-bay.styles: Single style: still, crisp, aromatic white made from 100% Nova Scotia grapes of approved varieties (2024 releases blend L'Acadie Blanc, Seyval Blanc, Vidal, Geisenheim 318, New York Muscat, Ortega, Frontenac and others), at most 11% abv.
ca-tidal-bay.labelling: Appellation launched June 2012 by Wine Growers Nova Scotia; each wine approved yearly by an independent blind tasting panel. A trade standard, not provincial law.

ca-vin-de-glace-du-quebec.varieties: Any white or red variety except pure Vitis labrusca (Vidal most widely used).
ca-vin-de-glace-du-quebec.min_alcohol: 7 to 14.9% abv; residual sugar at least 125 g/l; VA max 2.1 g/l; total SO2 max 420 mg/l.
ca-vin-de-glace-du-quebec.styles: Grapes frozen naturally on the vine, or bunches detached after a hard freeze and kept in continuous nets on their own vines (protects buried, non-hardy vines); harvest and pressing at an outside temperature of minus 8 C or colder after several freeze-thaw cycles; at least 32 Brix at each pressing and 35 Brix in tank before fermentation. No chaptalisation, fortification or artificial freezing at any stage. Still or sparkling (tank or traditional method).
ca-vin-de-glace-du-quebec.labelling: IGP reserved 30 December 2014. Pressing, vinification, ageing and bottling at the vineyard inside the delimited area; must bought in only from certified growers who press on their own site.

ca-vin-du-quebec.varieties: Hybrid, vinifera and hardy (rustique) varieties grown in the delimited Quebec area; pure Vitis labrusca excluded.
ca-vin-du-quebec.min_alcohol: Still and sparkling wines 8 to 15% abv.
ca-vin-du-quebec.styles: White, red, rose, sparkling and semi-sparkling, late harvest, selective late harvest and dried-grape (passerille) wines; sweet wines at least 50 g/l residual sugar.
ca-vin-du-quebec.labelling: IGP recognised 17 November 2018 (English "Quebec Wine"). Vintage means at least 85% from that year. Single variety 85%; two varieties named with at least 15% of the second. Every wine is tasted by an approval committee; certified by an accredited body under CARTV.

region-ca-british-columbia.varieties: BC VQA: listed varieties (Schedule 3); Vitis vinifera only for VQA sparkling. BC Wine of Distinction: BC-grown grapes, no 100% labrusca wines, at most 5% from the listed non-labrusca hybrids.
region-ca-british-columbia.min_alcohol: Minimum Brix at harvest: table wine 18 (sub-regional GIs) or 17 (British Columbia); Late Harvest 23, Select Late Harvest 26, Special Select Late Harvest 32, Botrytis Affected 26, Totally Botrytis Affected 34; Vin du Cure 20 at harvest and 32 after drying; Icewine 32 per pressing and 35 average. Chaptalisation max 2.5% abv for regional GIs, 3.5% for British Columbia. Table wine 7 to 20%; VQA sparkling at least 8.5%.
region-ca-british-columbia.styles: Table, Icewine, Sparkling Icewine, Late Harvest (and Select, Special Select, Botrytis Affected, Totally Botrytis Affected), Vin du Cure, Meritage (Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Malbec, Petit Verdot, St. Macaire, Gros Verdot, Carmenere; white Sauvignon Blanc, Semillon, Sauvignon Vert; none above 90%), Solera (at least three barrels of different vintages, max 30% drawn yearly), Traditional Method Sparkling (at least 9 months on lees, 12 for vintage), Methode Cuvee Close (6 months), Aromatic Sparkling, Blanc de Noirs, Nouveau, Fortified, Liqueur.
region-ca-british-columbia.labelling: "British Columbia": 100% BC grapes. A regional or sub-regional GI: 85% from that GI and the rest from elsewhere in BC (lowered from 95% by B.C. Reg. 118/2025, effective 14 July 2025). Sub-GIs (e.g. Naramata Bench, Golden Mile Bench, Skaha Bench, Cowichan Valley) must also show their parent GI. Varietal 85%; two varieties 90% with at least 13.5% of the second; three 95% with 14.25% and 9.5%. Vintage 85%. Vineyard name: 100% from it. BC VQA "Estate Bottled": own or leased land (lease of at least 10 years, from its fourth year) in a regional GI, crushed, made and bottled on site. VQA wines pass a sensory panel and are bottled in glass within 90 days of it.
region-ca-british-columbia.sweetness: Still: Dry up to 4 g/l (or acid plus 2, max 9), Medium Dry up to 12 (or acid plus 10, max 18), Semi-Sweet 12 to 45, Sweet 45 to 100. Sparkling: Natural Brut up to 5 with no sweetened dosage, Brut up to 15, Extra Dry 15 to 25, Dry 25 to 35, Medium Dry 35 to 50, Sweet over 50.

src.title: B.C. Reg. 168/2018 Wines of Marked Quality Regulation, consolidated to 20 Oct 2026 (last amended by B.C. Reg. 118/2025)

region-ca-ontario.varieties: Viticultural area wines: vinifera only (Appendix B Table 1), except Vidal for Icewine. "Ontario" wines may use listed hybrids (Baco Noir, Marechal Foch, Vidal and others) but only as varietal wines.
region-ca-ontario.min_alcohol: Minimum average Brix at harvest, e.g. Cabernet Sauvignon 19.0 (Ontario) / 20.0 (viticultural area), Chardonnay 18.0/20.0, Pinot Noir 18.5/19.5, Merlot 19.0/20.5, Riesling 17.0/17.0; every component at least 17.0 Brix. Table wine 7.0 to 14.9% actual. Chaptalisation max 2.5% abv (42.5 g/l sugar) for viticultural areas, 3.5% (60.5 g/l) for Ontario.
region-ca-ontario.styles: Table wine; Icewine; Botrytized (B.A.) and Totally Botrytized (T.B.A.); Late Harvest (22 Brix), Select Late Harvest (26 average), Special Select Late Harvest (30 average); Vin de Cure or Appassimento (at least 85% of grapes dried for at least 30 days at 5 to 18 C to 26 Brix, 7 to 20%); Nouveau red (partial carbonic maceration); Blanc de Noirs; fortified and liqueur wine (over 14.9 to 20%); Sparkling Wine Traditional Method (at least 9 months on lees, 12 for vintage), Methode Cuve Close/Charmat, Sparkling Icewine, Icewine Dosage (at least 10% Icewine as dosage, 20 g/l sugar) and Fracette (Icewine tirage liqueur, max 15 g/l); Meritage (Bordeaux red or white varieties, none above 90%).
region-ca-ontario.labelling: "Ontario" VQA: 100% Ontario grapes, made and finished in Ontario. Viticultural areas (Niagara Peninsula, Lake Erie North Shore, Prince Edward County): 85% from the area. Regional areas (Niagara-on-the-Lake, Niagara Escarpment, West Niagara): 85% from it, rest from Niagara Peninsula. Sub-appellations (Four Mile Creek, St. David's Bench, Beamsville Bench, Twenty Mile Bench, Short Hills Bench, Vinemount Ridge, Lincoln Lakeshore, Creek Shores, Niagara River, Niagara Lakeshore, South Islands): 100%. Single varietal 85%; two varieties 90% together with at least 15% of the second; three 95% with 15% and 10%. Vintage 85% and mandatory except sparkling, fortified, liqueur and Ontario-only table wine. Vineyard name: 100% from it. Estate Bottled: own or controlled land in a viticultural area (not in the first three years of a lease), made and bottled on site. "VQA" must flank the geographical indication in the same type size. Every wine passes a VQA tasting panel.
region-ca-ontario.sweetness: Sparkling: Natural Brut up to 15 g/l with no sweetened dosage, Brut up to 15, Extra Dry 15 to 25, Dry 25 to 35, Medium Dry 35 to 50, Sweet over 50. Fortified and liqueur: Dry up to 30, Medium Dry 30 to 65, Sweet over 65. Icewine: Sweet, over 100 g/l with at least 6.5 g/l acidity.
region-ca-ontario.other: Sweet reserve max 15% of volume and counted in varietal and vintage percentages. No water to stretch yield; no fortification outside the fortified category. Glass bottle by default; PET, aluminium, steel or multilayer allowed with fill date; "Estate Bottled" and "fermented in this bottle" only on glass.
